mentions.name: Integrated AI-powered Firefox fork
mentions.description: This is a custom Firefox fork that strips out unwanted Mozilla features (Firefox sync, VPN), reworks the UX/UI, and integrates mail, calendar, a Notion-like document library, native ad-blocking, a terminal, Trello-style task tracking, and Harvest-style time tracking into the browser. It embeds AI (Apple Intelligence on macOS and Claude) to search the web on a schedule and email custom daily briefs, maintain a queryable memory of work across multiple clients, pull and cohesively format analytics from multiple web dashboards, program the web via a node-based infinite canvas with live websites in the workflow, and automatically update tasks from activity like sent emails, replacing the need to keep half a dozen applications open.
mentions.problem: Juggling half a dozen separate applications for daily work, plus unwanted Mozilla features and UX/UI choices the author finds poorly handled upstream.
mentions.audience: Personal use for the builder's own multi-client work
mentions.source_excerpt:
I've started maintaining my own Firefox fork that:

- removes the stuff that I don't care about (Firefox sync, VPN, etc.)

- fixes a lot of the awful UX/UI choices that the (frankly) incompetent product team at Mozilla refuse to

- actually adds stuff that I do like integrated mail and calendar, a document library system (basically Notion), native ad-blocking, terminal, task-tracking like Trello, time-tracking like Harvest, etc.
mentions.author: ramijames
